# react-liquid-theme

> Build Shopify theme `.liquid` files from React (TSX) components. Components are rendered ONCE at build time
> (in Node, via `react-dom/server`) into Liquid templates. React never runs in the browser. Liquid logic is
> written as strings passed to `Liquid*` components; Shopify evaluates it at request time.

This file is a guide for AI assistants writing code in a project that uses `react-liquid-theme`.

## Mental model

- A `*.snippet.tsx` file's default export is a React component with NO props. It is rendered to static markup,
  formatted with Prettier, and written to `theme/snippets/<name>.liquid`.
- There is no runtime React: no state, effects, event handlers, context from the page, or props from Shopify.
  `useState`, `onClick`, etc. do nothing useful. Dynamic data comes from Liquid (`product.title`, `section.settings.x`).
- JS values are evaluated at build time. `{items.map(...)}` over a JS array unrolls into static HTML;
  `<LiquidFor statement="item in collection.products">` loops at request time in Shopify.
- Interactivity goes in a sibling `*.client.ts` file (plain DOM / custom elements), bundled into `theme/assets/main.js`.
- Reusable React components in non-suffixed files (e.g. `src/components/button.tsx`) are inlined into every file that
  imports them. Use `LiquidRender` + a snippet instead when the markup should exist once in the theme.

## Exports

```ts
// Liquid components + schema helpers + JSON helpers + decoding helpers
import { LiquidIf, LiquidFor, LiquidExpression, LiquidRender, LiquidSchema, defineSectionSchema, defineBlockSchema,
         LiquidJson, liquid, liquidString, when, each, raw, toLiquidJson,
         HtmlDecoder, makeDecodable } from 'react-liquid-theme'
import { defineJsxTag } from 'react-liquid-theme/utils' // custom element tag names in JSX
import { defineOptions } from 'react-liquid-theme/config' // theme.config.js
```

`src/global.d.ts` must contain `/// <reference types="react-liquid-theme/declarations" />` (types for CSS/SCSS
imports, `import.meta.env` and CSS custom properties in `style`).

## File naming -> theme output

Files are discovered under the source dir (default `src`, any depth). Pattern: `<name>.<type>.tsx|ts`.
Output file name is `<name>` (everything before `.<type>`); subfolders are flattened, so names must be unique per type.

| Source                      | Output                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `hero.section.tsx`          | `theme/sections/hero.liquid`    |
| `card.snippet.tsx`          | `theme/snippets/card.liquid`    |
| `product.template.tsx`      | `theme/templates/product.liquid`|
| `theme.layout.tsx`          | `theme/layout/theme.liquid`     |
| `group.block.tsx`           | `theme/blocks/group.liquid`     |
| `settings_schema.config.ts` | `theme/config/settings_schema.<ext>` (see `fileInfo`) |
| `en.default.locale.ts`      | `theme/locales/en.default.<ext>`|
| `foo.asset.ts`              | `theme/assets/foo.<ext>`        |
| `card.snippet.client.ts`    | bundled into `theme/assets/main.js` |
| `showroom.sections.tsx`     | one `theme/sections/<key>.liquid` per key of the default export |

A section and a snippet may share a name (`perks.section.tsx` + `perks.snippet.tsx`). Two sources that map to the
same output (e.g. `a/hero.section.tsx` and `b/hero.section.tsx`) fail the build with an error.

Client files MUST be named `<name>.<type>.client.ts(x)` (`.client` right before the extension) and only get bundled
when a matching server file (`<name>.<type>.tsx`) exists.

### Several outputs from one file

`<name>.sections.tsx`, `.snippets.tsx`, `.blocks.tsx` and `.templates.tsx` export an object as default; every key is
an output file name (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`) and every value a component. The source name is not used.

```tsx
// src/showroom.sections.tsx -> theme/sections/showroom-paris.liquid, theme/sections/showroom-rome.liquid
const showroom = (city: string) => () => (
  <>
    <section>{city}</section>
    <LiquidSchema schema={defineSectionSchema({ name: `Showroom ${city}` })} />
  </>
)
export default { 'showroom-paris': showroom('Paris'), 'showroom-rome': showroom('Rome') }
```

### Non-Liquid outputs (`fileInfo`)

A file can export `fileInfo` to change the output extension and render mode:

```ts
// src/settings_schema.config.ts -> theme/config/settings_schema.json
export const fileInfo = { extension: 'json', renderType: 'string' }
export default function () {
  return JSON.stringify([{ name: 'theme_info', theme_name: 'My theme' }], null, 2)
}
```

- `renderType: 'jsx'` (default): default export is a component, rendered to Liquid/HTML.
- `renderType: 'string'`: default export is a function returning the file content as a string (written as is).
- `extension` defaults to `'liquid'`.

## Writing Liquid in JSX

### Rule: never put Liquid with quotes or `<`, `>`, `&` in plain JSX text or attributes

React HTML-escapes strings. `{"{{ 'x' | t }}"}` renders as `{{ &#x27;x&#x27; | t }}`, which is broken Liquid.

```tsx
// text output: use LiquidExpression
<h1><LiquidExpression expression="'general.title' | t" /></h1>

// attributes: plain strings are fine only with no quotes / special chars
<a href="{{ product.url }}">...</a>
// otherwise wrap the value in makeDecodable
<img alt={makeDecodable("{{ product.title | escape }}")} src={makeDecodable("{{ image | image_url: width: 600 }}")} />

// any other raw Liquid/HTML string that must not be escaped
<HtmlDecoder>{"{{ 'a' | append: \"b\" }}"}</HtmlDecoder>
```

Conditions/statements passed to `Liquid*` components are never escaped, so `condition="a > b and c == 'd'"` is fine.

### Control flow

```tsx
<LiquidIf condition="product.available">
  <span>In stock</span>
  <LiquidElseIf condition="product.tags contains 'preorder'">
    <span>Preorder</span>
  </LiquidElseIf>
  <LiquidElse>
    <span>Sold out</span>
  </LiquidElse>
</LiquidIf>
```

`LiquidElseIf`, `LiquidElse` and `LiquidWhen` are placed INSIDE the parent (`LiquidIf`/`LiquidUnless`/`LiquidCase`).
They emit their tag followed by their children; nothing closes them.

```tsx
<LiquidCase variable="section.settings.layout">
  <LiquidWhen value="'grid'"><Grid /></LiquidWhen>
  <LiquidWhen value="'list', 'stack'"><List /></LiquidWhen>
  <LiquidElse><Fallback /></LiquidElse>
</LiquidCase>

<LiquidFor statement="product in collection.products limit: 4">
  <LiquidRender statement="'product-card', product: product" />
  <LiquidIf condition="forloop.index == 2"><LiquidBreak /></LiquidIf>
</LiquidFor>
```

### Component reference

Block tags (wrap children, emit `{% x %}...{% endx %}`):

| Component        | Props                     | Output                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `LiquidIf`       | `condition`               | `{% if condition %}...{% endif %}`        |
| `LiquidUnless`   | `condition`               | `{% unless condition %}...{% endunless %}`|
| `LiquidCase`     | `variable`                | `{% case variable %}...{% endcase %}`     |
| `LiquidFor`      | `statement`               | `{% for statement %}...{% endfor %}`      |
| `LiquidTablerow` | `statement`               | `{% tablerow statement %}...` (inside `<table>`) |
| `LiquidCapture`  | `variableName`            | `{% capture variableName %}...`           |
| `LiquidComment`  | -                         | `{% comment %}...{% endcomment %}`        |
| `LiquidRawTag`   | -                         | `{% raw %}...{% endraw %}`                |
| `LiquidTag`      | `name`, `statement?`      | `{% name statement %}...{% endname %}` (any block tag: `form`, `paginate`, `schema`, `style`, `javascript`, ...) |

Single tags:

| Component             | Props                  | Output                               |
| --------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `LiquidElseIf`        | `condition`, children  | `{% elsif condition %}` + children   |
| `LiquidElse`          | children               | `{% else %}` + children              |
| `LiquidWhen`          | `value`, children      | `{% when value %}` + children        |
| `LiquidAssign`        | `name`, `value`        | `{% assign name = value %}`          |
| `LiquidEcho`          | `expression`           | `{% echo expression %}`              |
| `LiquidRender`        | `statement`, or `snippet`, `args?`, `with?`/`for?`, `as?` | `{% render 'snippet' with x as y, key: value %}` |
| `LiquidInclude`       | same as `LiquidRender` (no `for`) | `{% include ... %}` (deprecated, for legacy themes) |
| `LiquidSection`       | `name`                 | `{% section 'name' %}`               |
| `LiquidSections`      | `name`                 | `{% sections 'name' %}`              |
| `LiquidCycle`         | `values: string[]`, `group?` | `{% cycle group: v1, v2 %}`    |
| `LiquidIncrement`     | `variableName`         | `{% increment variableName %}`       |
| `LiquidDecrement`     | `variableName`         | `{% decrement variableName %}`       |
| `LiquidInlineComment` | `comment`              | `{% # comment %}`                    |
| `LiquidBreak`         | -                      | `{% break %}`                        |
| `LiquidContinue`      | -                      | `{% continue %}`                     |
| `LiquidSelfClosingTag`| `name`, `statement?`   | `{% name statement %}` (any single tag: `content_for`, `layout`, ...) |
| `LiquidExpression`    | `expression`           | `{{ expression }}`                   |
| `LiquidStatement`     | `statement` (multiline)| `{% liquid statement %}`             |

`LiquidRender` args are Liquid expressions: `args={{ image: 'section.settings.image', size: "'large'" }}`;
`undefined` values are skipped. The snippet name is a plain string (`snippet="card"`), quotes are added.

Other:

- `LiquidRaw` (`liquid: string`): parses an HTML/Liquid string into React elements. Text inside it is still escaped,
  so quoted Liquid in text breaks; prefer `HtmlDecoder` for verbatim strings.
- `LiquidJson` / `LiquidScript`: see below.
- All values (`condition`, `statement`, `value`, ...) are raw Liquid source strings. String literals need Liquid quotes:
  `value="'grid'"`, `name="title" value="'Hello'"`.

### Whitespace control

Single tags and `LiquidExpression`: `leftTrim` -> `{%-` / `{{-`, `rightTrim` -> `-%}` / `-}}`.

Block tags have two tags, so four flags:

- `leftTrim`: `{%-` on the opening tag
- `leftBeginTrim`: `-%}` on the opening tag
- `rightTrim`: `{%-` on the closing tag
- `rightBeginTrim`: `-%}` on the closing tag

## Sections: `{% schema %}`

```tsx
// src/hero.section.tsx
import { defineSectionSchema, LiquidExpression, LiquidSchema } from 'react-liquid-theme'

const schema = defineSectionSchema({
  name: 'Hero',
  settings: [
    { type: 'text', id: 'title', label: 'Title', default: 'Welcome' },
    { type: 'range', id: 'margin', label: 'Margin', min: 0, max: 100, step: 4, unit: 'px', default: 20 },
  ],
  blocks: [{ type: '@app' }, { type: 'slide', name: 'Slide', settings: [] }],
  presets: [{ name: 'Hero' }],
})

export default function HeroSection() {
  return (
    <>
      <section className="hero">
        <h1><LiquidExpression expression="section.settings.title | escape" /></h1>
      </section>
      <LiquidSchema schema={schema} />
    </>
  )
}
```

- `defineSectionSchema` (sections) / `defineBlockSchema` (theme blocks) return the schema unchanged; they exist for
  type checking: unknown setting types, misspelled keys, missing required keys (`range` needs `min`/`max`/`default`),
  unknown templates in `enabled_on`/`disabled_on`.
- Types are exported too: `SectionSchema`, `ThemeBlockSchema`, `Setting`, `SettingType`, `SchemaPreset`, ...
- `LiquidSchema` accepts any object. Without it, write
  `<LiquidTag name="schema"><HtmlDecoder>{JSON.stringify(schema)}</HtmlDecoder></LiquidTag>` (`HtmlDecoder` is required,
  otherwise the JSON quotes are HTML-escaped).

## `<script>` with Liquid

React only allows one string inside `<script>`, so Liquid components cannot be nested in a plain `<script>`.

`LiquidJson` builds JSON from a JS object; helpers mark the dynamic parts:

```tsx
<LiquidJson
  type="application/ld+json"
  value={{
    '@type': 'Product',
    name: liquid('product.title'),                         // {{ product.title | json }}
    availability: when('product.available', 'InStock', 'OutOfStock'),
    sku: when('product.selected_or_first_available_variant.sku != blank',
              liquid('product.selected_or_first_available_variant.sku')), // key omitted if falsy
    offers: each('variant in product.variants',
                 { price: liquid('variant.price | divided_by: 100.0') },
                 { setup: 'assign ok = variant.available', where: 'ok' }),
    related: raw("{% render 'related-json' %}"),           // Liquid that already outputs JSON
  }}
/>
```

- `liquid(expr)` -> `{{ expr | json }}` (do not add `| json` yourself)
- `liquidString(expr)` -> the printed output of `{{ expr }}` as a JSON string (via `{% capture %}` + `| json`). Use it
  for filters that print a Liquid error on bad input (`image_url` on a missing image): `liquid()` would put the error
  outside the quotes and break the JSON. For optional values, combine with `when()`:
  `image: when('product.featured_image', liquidString('product.featured_image | image_url: width: 800'))`
- `when(cond, then)` -> key/array item omitted when falsy (`null` if used as a bare value)
- `when(cond, then, otherwise)` -> either value
- `each(statement, item, { setup?, where? })` -> JSON array from `{% for %}`; `where` skips iterations
- `raw(liquid)` -> inserted as is
- Plain JS values are serialized and escaped at build time. Commas are handled automatically.
- `toLiquidJson(value)` returns the same Liquid as a string.

`LiquidScript` for arbitrary JS, with a string `value` or Liquid component children (not both):

```tsx
<LiquidScript value={`window.product = {{ product | json }}`} />
<LiquidScript value={`window.data = ${toLiquidJson({ id: liquid('product.id') })}`} />
<LiquidScript>
  {'window.ids = ['}
  <LiquidFor statement="p in products">
    <LiquidExpression expression="p.id" />
    <LiquidUnless condition="forloop.last">,</LiquidUnless>
  </LiquidFor>
  {']'}
</LiquidScript>
```

## Client-side JS

```tsx
// src/counter.snippet.tsx
import { defineJsxTag } from 'react-liquid-theme/utils'
const AppCounter = defineJsxTag('app-counter') // typed as 'div' so JSX accepts it; use data-* for custom attrs

export default function CounterSnippet() {
  return <AppCounter data-start="{{ start | default: 0 }}"><button type="button">+</button></AppCounter>
}
```

```ts
// src/counter.snippet.client.ts  -> bundled into theme/assets/main.js
class AppCounter extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() { /* ... */ }
}
customElements.define('app-counter', AppCounter)
```

- All client files are bundled into one ESM file (`main.js` by default, browser target, minified). The theme must load
  it (e.g. `<script src="{{ 'main.js' | asset_url }}" type="module" defer></script>` in the layout).
- Prefer vanilla DOM / custom elements. JSX in client files compiles against `preact`, which is NOT bundled.
- Client files run only in the browser; server files run only in Node at build time. Browser APIs (`window`,
  `HTMLElement`) must not be touched in server files.

## Styles

- Import `.css`, `.scss`, `.module.css`, `.module.scss` from any server or client file.
- All imported CSS is concatenated into `theme/assets/main.css` (name set by `--css`). The theme must include it
  (`{{ 'main.css' | asset_url | stylesheet_tag }}`).
- CSS modules: `import classes from './card.module.scss'` -> `classes.root` is the scoped class name (`root__<n>`).
- SCSS files get a global `$env` map built from the `.env` file, and `~pkg/path` imports resolve from `node_modules`.

CSS custom properties work in `style` without casts: `style={{ '--gap': '1rem', color: 'red' }}`.

## Environment variables

Values from `.env` (path set by `--env`) are inlined as `import.meta.env.KEY` in server and client files
(only keys that are valid JS identifiers).

## CLI and config

```bash
npx react-liquid-theme setup              # scaffold package.json scripts, tsconfig, example snippet
npx react-liquid-theme generate           # build once
npx react-liquid-theme generate --watch   # rebuild on change (only changed files are rewritten)
```

Options (CLI flags override `theme.config.js`):

| Option   | Default         | Meaning                                       |
| -------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `source` | `src`           | React source dir                              |
| `dist`   | `.react-liquid` | intermediate JS build (gitignore it)          |
| `theme`  | `theme`         | Shopify theme dir that receives output        |
| `css`    | `main.css`      | CSS bundle name in `theme/assets`             |
| `js`     | `main.js`       | client JS bundle name in `theme/assets`       |
| `env`    | `.env`          | env file                                      |
| `sassSilenceDeprecations` | - | config file only, passed to Sass        |
| `htmlWhitespaceSensitivity` | `css` | config file only, prettier option for the output. `css` never changes rendered whitespace; `ignore` (pre-1.1 behavior) can turn `<a>Terms</a>.` into "Terms ." |

```js
// theme.config.js
import { defineOptions } from 'react-liquid-theme/config'
export default defineOptions({ theme: 'shopify-theme' })
```

Recommended `tsconfig.json`: `{ "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "preserve", "module": "preserve",
"moduleResolution": "bundler", "skipLibCheck": true, "target": "esnext" } }`. Project must be ESM (`"type": "module"`).

## Rules of thumb for AI assistants

1. Never edit generated files in the theme dir (they start with an `AUTO-GENERATED` comment naming
   the source file to edit); edit that file in `src/` instead.
2. Liquid text output -> `LiquidExpression`; Liquid in attributes with quotes -> `makeDecodable`.
3. Liquid string literals inside props need their own quotes: `condition="handle == 'home'"`.
4. Use JS (`map`, constants, helper components) for things known at build time, Liquid components for things
   known only at request time.
5. No React runtime features (hooks, event handlers, props on the default export).
6. Reach for `LiquidTag` / `LiquidSelfClosingTag` for any Liquid tag without a dedicated component.
7. Sections: `defineSectionSchema` + `<LiquidSchema schema={schema} />`. Render calls with several arguments:
   `<LiquidRender snippet="x" args={{ ... }} />` instead of building the statement string by hand.
